title: The finite key effect of side-channel-secure quantum key distribution beyond post-selection technique
authors: Cong Jiang, Zong-Wen Yu, Xiang-Bin Wang
abstract: By applying the framework of entropic uncertainty relation (EUR) and the Quantum Leftover Hash Lemma (QLHL), we introduce a security-proof method for variable-length side-channel-secure (SCS) quantum key distribution (QKD) against coherent attacks. This method reframes composable security as a statistical fluctuation problem of phase errors, enabling direct proofs against coherent attacks through observables and virtual observables. It yields tight key rates for the SCS protocol and reduces pulse requirements by over two orders of magnitude compared to prior works that employ the post-selection technique. We prove that the secure key length for the SCS protocol can be determined after error correction by exploiting the fact that untagged bits are free from bit-flip errors, using the actual information leakage during error correction and the post-error-correction statistics of each state to calculate the final key rate. We further identify sufficient conditions under which the final key length may be determined after error correction in a broader class of QKD protocols. Under the framework of EUR and QLHL, we clarify the applicability of several commonly used concentration bounds to variable-length QKD and the appropriate manner of their implementation. This work enhances the practical value of the SCS protocol and clarifies the security justification of key-rate formulas used in practical variable-length QKD implementations.
summary: This paper presents a security-proof method for variable-length Side-Channel-Secure Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) that bypasses the need for restrictive post-selection techniques. By utilizing Entropic Uncertainty Relations, it derives tight key rates directly from observed statistical fluctuations during error correction. This significantly enhances the practical applicability and theoretical justification of modern QKD protocols.
main_problem: Developing a security-proof method for variable-length side-channel-secure (SCS) Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) that avoids the limitations of post-selection techniques.
main_result: The authors introduce a novel framework using Entropic Uncertainty Relations and the Quantum Leftover Hash Lemma to derive tight, direct key rates for SCS-QKD against coherent attacks.
method: The security analysis reframes composable security as a statistical fluctuation problem of phase errors, allowing the calculation of the secure key length based on actual information leakage during error correction.
model_or_system: The study focuses on the Side-Channel-Secure (SCS) QKD protocol, involving two senders (Alice and Bob) transmitting quantum states to an untrusted measurement party Charlie. The analysis also touches upon variable-length BB84 protocols using decoy states.
key_observables: Phase-error rate, counting rates of distinct quantum states ($ho_{oA k}, ho_{xAk}$), and the final key length $\ell_{i,h}$.
important_parameters: The protocol's security is characterized by parameters derived from observed counts and error correction leakage.
main_assumptions: Initial analysis assumes no bit-dependent correlation between emitted pulses and that Eve cannot enter the laboratory; later sections analyze applicability to broader QKD classes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first introducing the SCS-QKD protocol framework, then detailing the mathematical tools (EUR, QLHL) used for security proofs, and finally extending these techniques to clarify key-rate formulas applicable across various variable-length QKD implementations.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous theoretical advancements in quantum cryptography by developing new methods to calculate secure key rates that are more practical and robust than previous post-selection based approaches.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Comparison of key rates with diﬀerent N. The curves show the secret key rate (bits per pulse) versus ﬁber distance (km) for total pulse numbers N = 1011, 1012, and 1014. Our method outperforms prior works, enabling secure QKD at longer distances with fewer pulses.

FIG. 2. Comparison of key rates with diﬀerent ed. The curves show the secret key rate (bits per pulse) versus ﬁber distance (km) for the misalignment-error probability ed = 3%, 4%, 5%, 6% and 7%. High ed is commonly observed in both deployed ﬁeld ﬁber links and free-space channels. The results shows that the maximum transmission distance of the SCS protocol decreases only mildly with increasing ed.
